## 🔀 Blocked — velo won't build once the MCP toolkit is switched on
**Needs:** answer

@pmcp the code is written and all the new tests pass. One thing the plan didn't cover stops velo from building. Every crouton app gets `nuxt-ai-ready` through crouton-core (`@nuxtjs/seo`). When that module sees `@nuxtjs/mcp-toolkit`, it tries to add its own "site tools" to it, and those need a database plus `drizzle-orm` 1.0 rc. velo has 0.45.4, so `nuxt typecheck` stops:

```
[nuxt-ai-ready] These features need the database: MCP site tools (`@nuxtjs/mcp-toolkit`).
The database needs `drizzle-orm` ^1.0.0-rc.4. This app installs 0.45.4.
```

The fix is one setting, `aiReady: { mcp: { tools: false, resources: false } }`. It stops nuxt-ai-ready from adding tools, so it needs no database (from its source: `mcpNeedsDatabase` is false when both are `false`). The approved plan says to stop when reality differs, so I'm asking where that setting should go.

**My recommendation: A.** Set it inside the toolkit module as a default (`defu`, so an app can still override it). Then any app that turns the toolkit on builds, not just velo. It also keeps nuxt-ai-ready's own tools off `/mcp`.

A — set it as a default in the toolkit module (recommended)
B — set it only in `apps/velo/nuxt.config.ts`

A fresh run must not lose: the build is complete apart from this one setting (file list below). It only needs to add that setting w
